title: How Dagobert Renouf grew to 73k Twitter followers: reply-first engagement, memes and stories
summary: An Indie Hackers interview on how Dagobert Renouf turned Twitter into Logology's main acquisition channel after a flopped launch. He stresses participation over marketing, relentless replying, social relationships, authentic storytelling and a personal brand. Note: the article is written by an interviewer, with only one short direct quote from Dagobert.

principles.text: Participate in communities before trying to market; it beats promotion when you have no audience.
Treat Twitter as a social platform: make friends who will cheer for you, not just publish content.
principles.quote: Twitter is not a content media platform. It's a SOCIAL media platform. You gotta be social and make friends who will cheer for you.

principles.text: Be consistent: post on a fixed schedule for years and batch the creative work monthly.
principles.quote: he has posted twice a day (1 text tweet, 1 meme) every day except Sundays for years.

principles.text: Engage heavily: aim for 50+ replies to others daily and answer everyone who comments on your posts.
principles.quote: He aimed for 50+ replies to other people's tweets, and then replied to everyone who commented on his.

principles.text: Source content ideas from the conversations you have; answering your audience beats inventing topics.
principles.quote: Replying to what your audience is asking is easier and more effective than dreaming up topics.

principles.text: Tell stories about your journey, not your product: problem, emotional pain, resolution and lesson.
principles.quote: He doesn't ever really talk about his product — he talks about his journey.
